Class LogProperty.Validator

java.lang.Object
io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProperty.Validator
Enclosing interface:
LogProperty
public static class LogProperty.Validator extends Object
Accumulates LogProperty.Results from one or more property lookups and validates them together, so that a caller resolving several properties in sequence can report every failure at once instead of failing fast on the first bad property.

This is the mechanism generated fromProperties(LogProperties) builder implementations use: each property is looked up and its LogProperty.Result is added to the validator as it is read; validate() is then called once at the end, after all properties have been read, so a user who misconfigured several properties sees all of the problems together rather than fixing them one at a time across repeated runs.

Use add(Result) for a property that is required: a LogProperty.Result.Missing is treated as a failure. Use addIfError(Result) for an optional property that already has a fallback applied (typically via LogProperty.Result.or(Object) with the builder's current field value): a LogProperty.Result.Missing is expected in that case and is silently ignored, but a LogProperty.Result.Error (the property was present but failed to convert) is still a real problem and is reported.

API Note
a Validator is single-use: create one with of(Class), add every result that should be checked, and call validate() exactly once at the end.

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static LogProperty.Validator of(Class<?> builder)
      Creates a validator whose LogProperty.ValidationException messages will be prefixed with the name of the given class.
      Parameters:
      builder - the class on whose behalf properties are being resolved - typically the builder calling this method. It is only used to identify the source of a failure in the exception message; no state is read from it.
      Returns:
      newly created validator.

    • add

      public LogProperty.Validator add(LogProperty.Result<?> result)
      Adds a result that must be present. Both LogProperty.Result.Missing and LogProperty.Result.Error will cause validate() to fail. Use this for a required property; for an optional property that already has a fallback value applied, use addIfError(Result) instead so a missing value does not itself trigger a failure.
      Parameters:
      result - result to check.
      Returns:
      this.

    • addIfError

      public LogProperty.Validator addIfError(LogProperty.Result<?> result)
      Adds a result only if it is a LogProperty.Result.Error; a LogProperty.Result.Missing result is silently ignored. Intended for an optional property that has already had a fallback value applied (for example via LogProperty.Result.or(Object)): the property being absent is expected and fine, but if it was present and failed to convert that should not be swallowed.
      Parameters:
      result - result to check.
      Returns:
      this.

    • validate

      public void validate() throws LogProperty.ValidationException
      Validates every result added so far via add(Result) or addIfError(Result), throwing a single exception listing all failures if one or more of them are not LogProperty.Result.Success.
      Throws:
      LogProperty.ValidationException - if any added result is a LogProperty.Result.Missing (added via add(Result)) or a LogProperty.Result.Error (added via either method).
